tema: Analyses whether physical deconditioning, measured by CPET, is related to orthostatic intolerance measured by CBF reduction in ME/CFS.
diseno: Study with 18 healthy controls and 122 ME/CFS patients without hypotension or tachycardia on the tilt test; % peak VO2 by CPET, CBF by extracranial Doppler and cardiac index by suprasternal Doppler.
hallazgos: Patients had lower % peak VO2 and greater CBF reduction than controls, but there was no relationship between the degree of deconditioning and the CBF reduction. Patients without abnormal CBF reduction showed cardiac index reductions intermediate between controls and patients with abnormal CBF, with no differences in %VO2.
conclusion: Deconditioning does not appear to play an important role in OI; cardiocerebral coupling could differ between ME/CFS subgroups.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the deconditioning-OI focus; the conclusions add the cardiocerebral coupling hypothesis, only implicit in the abstract.

tema: Explores, through hierarchical analysis of routine blood tests, whether ME/CFS subgroups can be identified.
diseno: Unbiased hierarchical cluster analysis in a cohort of 250 well-phenotyped women with ME/CFS.
hallazgos: Differences were observed in five blood parameters. 43% of participants (107 of 250) had high levels of complement factor C1q, which would define a subgroup with more pain.
conclusion: C1q would be a new player in the pathology of ME/CFS and opens the way to a laboratory assay to detect subtypes, although the underlying mechanism is still poorly understood.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on C1q, subtyping and pain. The conclusions also acknowledge that the mechanism is poorly understood, a nuance of caution that the abstract does not include; the abstract is partially truncated.

tema: Reviews the evidence for autoimmunity in CFS, POTS, CRPS and silicone implant incompatibility syndrome, proposing a unifying concept.
diseno: Narrative review of immunogenetics, autoimmune comorbidities, cell subpopulations, autoantibodies and animal models.
hallazgos: Autoantibodies against G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) and small fibre neuropathy are described in the four syndromes; Sjögren's syndrome serves as a model; a PET study showed lower receptor binding in CFS with anti-M1 antibodies.
conclusion: They propose the concept of autoimmune neurosensory dysautonomia to identify an autoimmune subgroup that could benefit from immunotherapy.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (autoantibodies, small fibre neuropathy, dysautonomia); the conclusions qualify that this would apply to at least a subgroup of patients.

tema: Comprehensive plasma metabolomic analysis in women with ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control with 52 women (half patients); about 1750 compounds in 20 super-pathways; statistical analysis and pathway enrichment.
hallazgos: Acylcholines consistently reduced in two cohorts; androgenic steroids, progestogens and corticoids reduced; fewer dipeptides and more sphingolipids.
conclusion: No unequivocal biomarker was identified, but acylcholines and steroids merit study; sampling during PEM could widen the differences.
triangulacion: Consistent on themes; the conclusions are more cautious in acknowledging the absence of a drastically different biomarker.

tema: To profile the gut DNA virome in severe ME/CFS and predict associated bacterial hosts.
diseno: Small cohort of severe patients and healthy controls from the same household; whole metagenomic sequencing (WMS) and virus-like particle (VLP) sequencing of stool; in silico host prediction. Exact size not stated.
hallazgos: Virome dominated by Caudoviricetes phages, with no differences in viral or bacterial alpha or beta diversity between groups; one vOTU assigned to smacovirus 1; Anaerotruncus would interact with viruses exclusive to patients.
conclusion: Provides a framework for studying virome-bacteriome interactions in ME/CFS in larger cohorts.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions (with methods noise) emphasize the absence of diversity differences, more cautious than the abstract's suggestion of dysbiosis.

tema: Adapts a chronic illness stigma scale to ME/CFS and confirms its factor structure.
diseno: Psychometric study with confirmatory factor analysis in 554 people with ME or CFS from an international sample.
hallazgos: The factors showed good internal consistency and good model fit; participants reported high levels of stigma, estrangement and disclosure.
conclusion: Professionals, colleagues, friends and family must collaborate to reduce stigmatization; they propose educational interventions for physicians, peer-led approaches, consensus on name and case definition, and non-stigmatizing treatments such as pacing.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent around stigma; the conclusions (from the discussion) extend the abstract with structural and interpersonal intervention proposals.

tema: Evaluates whether connectivity between the salience network, the DMN and subcortical nodes differs in ME/CFS and distinguishes the ICC and Fukuda classes.
diseno: Resting-state and task fMRI in 24 healthy controls and 42 patients (18 ICC and 24 Fukuda); mean functional connectivity between hubs of the salience network, DMN and subcortical regions.
hallazgos: At rest only two connections differed (Fukuda); in the task 10 connections differed (5 ICC, 5 Fukuda), none in common, eight with a salience hub. Salience connections with the hippocampus and the reticular activating system were stronger than in controls.
conclusion: The Fukuda and ICC classes derive from different mechanisms and may be considered different diseases; the alterations in salience, RAS and hippocampus agree with the cognitive problems and the sleep-wake cycle.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the salience network, DMN, hippocampus and RAS; the conclusions firmly state that they are different diseases and suggest that the reinforced connections could be compensatory.

tema: Evaluates whether exercise-induced alterations of muscle membrane excitability (M-wave) explain the reduction in maximal muscle strength in ME/CFS.
diseno: Retrospective study of two groups of patients with (n = 30) or without (n = 28) M-wave alterations after cycle ergometer exercise; maximal handgrip strength before and after exercise with EMG of the flexor digitorum longus; post-exercise symptom questionnaire.
hallazgos: In the group with alterations, M-wave amplitude decreased and its duration increased after exercise; resting grip strength was lower, fell after exercise and its changes correlated with those of the M-wave. PEM, fatigue, myalgia, headache and cognitive dysfunction were more frequent in this group.
conclusion: Post-exercise sarcolemmal fatigue could cause muscle failure, and maximal grip strength would be a simple, inexpensive index of performance and fatigability, with potential as a screening tool.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add the value of handgrip dynamometry as a screening tool. The keywords focus on the M-wave and strength, without mentioning PEM.

tema: Explores connectivity of the cortical autonomic network (CAN) and its relationship to ME/CFS symptoms.
diseno: Resting-state eyes-closed qEEG in 34 ME/CFS patients and 34 healthy controls; localization with eLORETA and lagged coherence in 7 frequency bands; DePaul Symptom Questionnaire.
hallazgos: The cognitive, affective and somatomotor symptom clusters were associated with adaptations in the temporality and homogeneity of the modular organization of the CAN.
conclusion: CAN topology could be key in symptom manifestation and a therapeutic target; eLORETA is promising, although more data and peripheral autonomic measures are required.
triangulacion: The abstract is truncated opening text (without results), so the findings depend on the conclusions from the discussion; keywords and conclusions are consistent on CAN, eLORETA and symptom clusters.

tema: Investigates cortical activity on resting EEG in relation to executive function and fatigue in CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with 50 CFS patients and 50 matched controls; 19-channel eyes-closed EEG, eLORETA localization, MFI-20 and FSS; SnPM correction.
hallazgos: Significant differences in the delta (1-3 Hz) bands, with mainly frontal sources, and beta-2 (19-21 Hz), in the medial and superior parietal lobe. Left frontal delta sources were associated with lower motivation.
conclusion: There is a pattern of global CNS hypoactivation in CFS, consistent with cognitive slowing, and eLORETA is a promising tool.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent (delta, frontal and parietal lobes); the conclusions interpret the results as global hypoactivation, somewhat beyond what is described in the abstract.

tema: Editorial commentary that assesses whether minocycline could be a 'magic bullet' for treating ME/CFS following an open-label trial by Miwa.
diseno: Opinion article/commentary on a prospective open-label study without a control group with minocycline; provides no own data.
hallazgos: Recalls that the phase III trial with rituximab showed no benefit and highlights that in Miwa's study 27% of subjects improved ≥2 points in functional status in 6 weeks, attributed to inhibition of microglial activation. Points out limitations such as the high number of dropouts and the absence of a control.
conclusion: Given the heterogeneity of ME/CFS, a single drug for everyone is unlikely; proposes stratifying patients by cause of onset, duration, history and psychosocial factors before evaluating treatments, including non-pharmacological ones.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on minocycline, neuroinflammation and microglia, but the discussion shifts the focus toward heterogeneity and patient stratification, more cautious than the title. The discussion text includes editorial noise (affiliations, DOI).

tema: Experimental study on the effect of the CFS diagnostic label on the social support that friends would give.
diseno: Experimental study on peer perceptions of the CFS label; sample size not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: The CFS label, when appropriately given by a physician, increased friends' intention to offer social support; possible gender differences are noted.
conclusion: The CFS label can legitimize the patient's experience in their social network; more research is needed before dismissing it as harmful.
triangulacion: Keywords (social support, gender differences) and conclusions are consistent; the abstract is opening text (cover page of the accepted manuscript) and provides no results, so the information depends on the conclusions.

tema: Letter asking whether endothelial dysfunction and vascular damage could contribute to pain, inflammation and PEM in ME/CFS.
diseno: Letter/opinion article by a single author (parent of a child with chronic illness), not based on formal research.
hallazgos: According to the discussion, fluid leakage due to endothelial dysfunction and the resulting tissue hypoxia could explain PEM; cortisol or other fluid-retaining mediators would explain PEM after cognitive exertion or stress, and elevated oestrogens could aggravate the leak. The delay in PEM could be due to the time of the hypoxic effect or to a biphasic reaction.
conclusion: More research is needed on the causes of endothelial dysfunction and damage (infection, inflammatory overreaction, 'crashes', mast cell activation, surgeries, microclots) and its treatment.
triangulacion: The abstract is not available (only generic DOAJ text); keywords, title and discussion are consistent around the endothelium and PEM, with an explicitly speculative character.

tema: To review the possible involvement of the kynurenine pathway in the pathophysiology of ME/CFS.
diseno: Narrative review on the pathology and management of ME/CFS and evidence of kynurenine pathway alterations.
hallazgos: The kynurenine pathway is involved in NAD(H) production, the immune response and neuroinflammation, processes linked to ME/CFS symptoms.
conclusion: The kynurenine pathway is a candidate for a key piece and its regulation could offer new management strategies.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions add context on the lack of diagnostic advances and the heterogeneity of previous studies.

tema: Reviews recent research on the biological basis of ME/CFS and its potential for developing a diagnostic test.
diseno: Narrative review integrating own molecular studies (including a preclinical study of patients with mass spectrometry proteomics) and complementary work from other groups.
hallazgos: Elevation of inflammatory and immune processes, ongoing neuroinflammation and decreased general metabolism and mitochondrial function are described, which would contribute to the relapsing-remitting course; possible molecular biomarkers emerge from this.
conclusion: Several promising biomarkers have been identified, but they require validation in large, multicentre cohorts and against diseases with similar features.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent on inflammation, metabolism and biomarkers. The discussion is more cautious than the abstract in stressing the need for validation; it includes noise from contributions and funding.

tema: Summarizes the available knowledge on the probable causes of ME/CFS, with attention to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
diseno: Review chapter described as a systematic literature review; detailed methodology not stated.
hallazgos: The most probable theories are the post-infectious cytokine cascade, alterations of the microbiota and the intestinal barrier, alterations of the brain-gut and brain-adrenal axes, persistent low-grade immune stimulation and chronic oxidative stress. Post-COVID fatigue could share the post-viral cytokine cascade.
conclusion: The aetiology is probably complex and multifactorial; more research is needed to find a diagnostic biochemical marker and a causal treatment. The pandemic has increased the visibility of the disease.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on aetiology, COVID-19 and absence of biomarkers. The conclusions specify the aetiological hypotheses that the abstract only announces; the abstract contains errors in acronyms (CFE, PE, IPC).

tema: Evaluates whether a cytokine panel can classify PASC, ME/CFS, post-treatment Lyme disease and post-vaccination PASC-like symptoms.
diseno: Classification study in 236 patients (64 PASC, 50 ME/CFS, 29 PTLD, 42 POVIP, in addition to acute COVID-19); panel of 14 cytokines/chemokines and CART decision tree.
hallazgos: The algorithm based on cytokine 'hubs' classified PASC, ME/CFS, POVIP and acute COVID-19 with a mean F1 of 0.61 and high specificity (94%).
conclusion: Correct classification of these inflammatory conditions with similar symptoms is crucial for diagnosis and treatment; targeting therapies to specific cytokines could be a precision medicine tool.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on chronic inflammation and differential diagnosis through CART. The PDF conclusions add the cytokine-targeted therapeutic approach and possible antigen persistence, not present in the abstract.

tema: Pilot study characterizing plasma extracellular vesicles and their cytokine content in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control: 35 patients and 35 controls matched for age, sex and BMI; vesicles analysed with NTA, TEM and western blot, and immunoassay of 45 cytokines in plasma and vesicles in a subgroup of 19.
hallazgos: Patients had more vesicles of 30-130 nm, with no differences in mean size or cytokine concentrations. The cytokine correlation networks were different, with 13 inverse correlations in patients' plasma driven by IP-10 (CXCL10).
conclusion: Alterations in cytokine networks would be further evidence of immune dysregulation; larger, stratified longitudinal studies are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on vesicles, cytokines and CXCL10. The PDF conclusions emphasize the lack of differences in concentrations and the limitations (a single sample, no analysis by sex or duration), so they are more cautious than the abstract.

tema: Looks for a cytokine signature associated with ME/CFS severity.
diseno: Case-control study with measurement of cytokines in blood. Sample size and methods not stated in the available fragment.
hallazgos: Seventeen cytokines showed an upward linear trend with severity, among them CCL11 (eotaxin-1), CXCL10, IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-7, IL-17F and leptin; 13 of them are pro-inflammatory. Only CXCL9 correlated inversely with the duration of fatigue.
conclusion: The authors interpret that pro-inflammatory cytokines contribute to symptoms and that the disease has a strong immune component.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (cytokines, severity, eotaxin). The abstract is truncated at the start and no conclusions are available, so triangulation is limited.

tema: Reanalyses, with a common framework, DNA methylation data in blood from patients with fibromyalgia and ME/CFS to reconcile discrepant results.
diseno: Secondary reanalysis of three previous genome-wide methylation studies (22 fibromyalgia patients and 127 with ME/CFS), with public GEO data and gene set enrichment analysis.
hallazgos: Methylation changes coincided only in part with those published, but the enrichment analyses were surprisingly consistent across datasets and pointed to physiological processes related to the symptoms of both syndromes.
conclusion: Methylation appears to be involved in the pathogenesis of fibromyalgia and ME/CFS, possibly of chronic pain, but better-controlled studies are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on methylation and epigenetics. The conclusions shift the focus toward chronic pain and are more cautious than the abstract, since they call for better-controlled studies.

tema: Explores for the first time the genome-wide DNA methylation modifications associated with ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study in PBMC with the Illumina HumanMethylation450 array, controlling for invariant and polymorphic probes; gene ontology and network analysis. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Differentially methylated genes related to the immune response, cellular metabolism and kinase activity were abundant. The immune cell regulation genes, the largest cluster, showed hypomethylation in promoters and regulatory elements.
conclusion: The data agree with multisystem and immune dysregulation and implicate DNA modifications in the pathology of ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree fully (methylome, promoter hypomethylation, immune cluster). The rest of the conclusions text is supplementary tables.

tema: Explores the genetics, epigenetics and protein expression of BDNF in patients with ME/CFS and comorbid fibromyalgia.
diseno: Repeated-measures study in 54 participants (28 with ME/CFS and fibromyalgia and 26 matched controls), with questionnaires, sensory tests, serum BDNF by ELISA and polymorphism and methylation by pyrosequencing, repeated 4 days apart.
hallazgos: Serum BDNF was higher in patients (mean difference of 3.31 ng/ml) and exon 9 methylation lower (-2.16%), mediated by the Val66Met polymorphism. Lower methylation predicted more serum BDNF, and this predicted symptoms and generalized hyperalgesia.
conclusion: Serum BDNF is elevated in ME/CFS with fibromyalgia, regulated by exon 9 methylation; altered BDNF levels could be a key mechanism of its pathophysiology.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (BDNF, methylation, Val66Met, comorbidity with fibromyalgia). The conclusions come from the abstract itself, so they offer no independent view.

tema: To compare antibody responses against gut microbiota flagellins in Crohn's disease and ME/CFS.
diseno: Conference abstract; PhIP-Seq of 344,000 peptides in 256 Crohn's patients, 40 with ME/CFS and matched control groups from the Netherlands and the UK.
hallazgos: Both diseases showed a greater anti-flagellin response (P<0.001); N-terminal binding to Lachnospiraceae flagellins similar, C-terminal binding more prevalent in Crohn's.
conclusion: Antibody binding to the N-terminal domain of flagellins could influence TLR5 activation in both diseases.
triangulacion: Minimal keywords (only the two diseases); no conclusions are available and the abstract is truncated.

tema: Explores damp and mould hypersensitivity syndrome and vaccination as risk factors for ME/CFS.
diseno: Interview-based cohort study of families (n = 81 cases, 53 girls and 28 boys according to the table) with diagnoses of ME/CFS, POTS, PANS, CRPS and combinations; the available abstract is only the header of the accepted manuscript.
hallazgos: The table shows that most cases had ME/CFS, alone or with POTS (30 cases with ME/CFS + POTS); an 11-year-old girl had a stroke after vaccination. No quantitative results on mould exposure are given.
conclusion: The authors argue that adequate assessment of risk factors would increase vaccine safety without compromising herd immunity.
triangulacion: The abstract provides no content (it is opening text of the manuscript), so triangulation is limited; the keywords (mould, indoor air quality, multiple chemical sensitivity) and the discussion with noise (conflicts, contributions, table) point to the same focus, but with no verifiable results.

tema: Doctoral thesis by publications on the characterization of PEM and its physiology in adults with ME/CFS and its clinical and legal application.
diseno: Thesis by compendium of eleven peer-reviewed publications since 2012 (University of Portsmouth).
hallazgos: The publications contributed to describing the signs and symptoms of PEM/PESE and its underlying physiology, and to applying that knowledge to clinical and legal issues.
conclusion: Important gaps remain in the understanding of PEM and ME/CFS; the publications form a stable foundation for future contributions.
triangulacion: There are no keywords; the abstract is opening text (cover and acknowledgements) and the conclusions are brief and general. Title and conclusions agree on the function-physiology axis of PEM.
